stem: Kiara compares daytime length around 22 December. Place N is far north of the Equator. Place E is on the Equator. Place S is far south of the Equator.

options.text: Around 22 December, place N has its shortest day; place E stays near 12 hours of day and night.
Around 22 December, place N has its longest day; place E has almost no daylight.
Around 22 December, the Northern Hemisphere's longest day occurs, as at the March equinox.
Around 22 December, place S has about 12 hours of daylight, like a pole on 21 June.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: In the Northern Hemisphere, about 22 December is the shortest day; near the Equator, day and night stay close to 12 hours.

teacher.key_rationale: Northern mid-latitudes have their shortest day around 22 December; the equator stays near 12 h. B reverses season extremes; C confuses solstice with equinox; D misstates southern day length and pole rules.
